summary: The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students. About 37 scholars a year receive four years of tuition, books, fees and full residence support — but only students nominated by their own secondary school can apply.
covers: Tuition, books and incidental fees for four years.
Full residence support for four years.
About 37 scholarships are awarded each year.
eligibility: International students who will need a Canadian study permit.
In the final year of secondary school in 2026–27, or graduated no earlier than June 2026, and starting a first undergraduate degree at U of T in September 2027.
Students already enrolled at a post-secondary institution are not eligible.
Your school must nominate you — each school can nominate one student a year.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counsellor or principal to nominate you by 9 October 2026.
Apply for admission to U of T by 16 October 2026.
Complete the Pearson Scholarship application by 6 November 2026.
Finalists are selected on academic excellence, creativity and leadership in their school and community.
watch_out: All three steps fall in October and November — far earlier than U of T's normal admission deadlines. Start talking to your school now.
One nomination per school means competition begins inside your own school.
U of T also has other entrance awards for international students; apply for admission even if you are not nominated.

faq.q: My school has never nominated anyone. Can it start now?
faq.a: Only verified schools can nominate: U of T verifies schools and sends them the nomination form each July. Ask your counsellor straight away whether your school is set up for this year.
U of T notifies Pearson Scholars from the end of January, and tells every nominee its decision by April.

faq.q: Can I apply if I start in January or am already at university?
faq.a: No. You must start at U of T in September 2027, and students already in post-secondary studies are not eligible.
